title: XXXV–XXXVII. Uses of the moral law before and after the fall
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): In ye state belonging toward integrity its use was ye norm belonging toward perfect obedience. — Ye use belonging toward ye moral law varies according toward ye human's state. — XXXVI. — In ye moral law ye use and abrogation stand as toward be noted. — XXXV. — that toward ye regenerate it may be a norm belonging toward life. — 4. — that it may be a herald belonging toward ye just judgment belonging toward God finally toward be exercised against them; — 3. — 3:24); — that it may be a pedagogue toward Christ (Gal. — 2. — 7:7); — 4:15; — 3:19-20; — that it may convict them belonging toward their sins (Rom. — 1. — After ye fall its use toward humans stands as:
pass_b_english: XXXV. In the moral law the use and abrogation are to be noted. XXXVI. The use of the moral law varies according to the human's state. In the state of integrity its use was the norm of perfect obedience.

After the fall its use toward humans is: 1. that it may convict them of their sins (Rom. 3:19-20; 4:15; 7:7); 2. that it may be a pedagogue to Christ (Gal. 3:24); 3. that it may be a herald of the just judgment of God finally to be exercised against them; 4. that for the regenerate it may be a norm of life.
source_text: XXXV. Est autem in lege morali notandus usus & abrogatio. XXXVI. Usus legis moralis variat secundum status hominis. Usus legis moralis in statu integritatis fuit norma perfectae obedientiae. XXXVI–XXXVII. Usus legis moralis erga homines post lapsum est 1. ut peccatorum suorum convincat, Rom. 3:19-20; 4:15; 7:7; 2. ut sit paedagogus ad Christum, Gal. 3:24; 3. ut sit nuncia iusti iudicii Dei adversus eos tandem exercendi; 4. ut renatis sit norma vitae.
